purpose: Close the EQ4 loophole in the earlier common-basis matchgate barrier. After the exact Tovey-style occurrence<=3 normalization, a universal local holographic route would only need to handle arity at most three. This theorem proves that EQ3 and OR3 alone already cannot be simultaneously transformed to matchgate signatures by one invertible 2x2 basis over C.

source_fact.statement: Every matchgate signature has a parity condition: its support is entirely even-weight or entirely odd-weight. For symmetric arity-3 signatures this parity condition is the only matchgate constraint needed for the contradiction below.
source_fact.reference: Cai, Fu, Guo, Williams, FKT is Not Universal — A Planar Holant Dichotomy for Symmetric Constraints, Theory of Computing Systems 66 (2022), Proposition 2.8.

setup.equality: EQ3=e0^(tensor 3)+e1^(tensor 3). Under S^(tensor 3), its symmetric Hamming-weight entries are [a^3+c^3, a^2 b+c^2 d, a b^2+c d^2, b^3+d^3].
setup.clause: OR3=[0,1,1,1]. Up to the common nonzero det(S)^(-3) scale, the dual basis is T=[[d,-b],[-c,a]].

lemma_eq3_forces_antidiagonal_ratio.statement: If S^(tensor 3) EQ3 satisfies either matchgate parity condition, then a,b,c,d are all nonzero and, with r=c/a and s=d/b, one has r=-s.
even_case: Even parity requires a^2 b+c^2 d=0 and b^3+d^3=0.
Invertibility forces a,b,c,d all nonzero. Thus r^2 s=-1 and s^3=-1.
Hence r^2=s^2, so r=+s or r=-s over C. But det(S)=ab(s-r) is nonzero, excluding r=s. Therefore r=-s.
odd_case: Odd parity requires a^3+c^3=0 and a b^2+c d^2=0.
Invertibility again forces a,b,c,d all nonzero. Thus r^3=-1 and r s^2=-1.
Hence s^2=r^2, so s=+r or s=-r. Nonzero determinant excludes s=r. Therefore s=-r, equivalently r=-s.

theorem.name: NO_COMMON_INVERTIBLE_BASIS_MAKES_EQ3_AND_OR3_BOTH_MATCHGATE
theorem.statement: Over C, there is no invertible 2x2 matrix S such that S^(tensor 3) EQ3 and (S^(-T))^(tensor 3) OR3 are both matchgate signatures.
proof: By matchgate parity, the transformed EQ3 must be even or odd. The preceding lemma therefore forces r=-s.
If transformed OR3 has even parity, its odd-weight layers require g1=0 and g3=0. But g3=4-3g1=4, contradiction.
If transformed OR3 has odd parity, its even-weight layers require g0=0 and g2=0. But g0=-4-3g2=-4, contradiction.
Thus neither OR3 parity is possible after any invertible basis that makes EQ3 parity-supported.

algorithmic_consequence.killed: A universal bounded-occurrence SAT algorithm obtained by one common invertible 2x2 holographic basis that turns every degree-3 equality and every OR3 clause into local matchgates, followed by ordinary FKT/matchgate contraction.
algorithmic_consequence.strengthening: The earlier v1.2 barrier no longer needs an EQ4 vertex. It already holds on the exact occurrence<=3 hard core.
